answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with receipt-staked work slots: every task claim must cite a hardware-attested execution receipt, and each receipt locks a small stake for one epoch. Picture validators lined up on a narrow terrace: timber is plentiful for building stairs, but the canyon crossing only admits one walker at a time per receipt. An attacker forging a thousand identities must still buy a thousand real receipts and lock a thousand stakes, so each clone costs as much as a legitimate agent earns back. Copying names is free; cloning receipts is not.
